Supervision and enforcement of the Act is accomplished by the Montana Department of State Lands through issuance of an annual mining permit to the individual mining operators. In addition, it is required that a comprehensive plan for surface reclamation and restoration be submitted and approved, along with certain other requirements, together with an adequate performance bond.
Violators of the provisions of this Act are subject to payment of a monetary civil penalty. A person who willfully violates these provisions will be found guilty of a misdemeanor and fined accordingly.

Repeated noncompliance of the operator with the requirements of the Act can result in suspension of the permit by the State.

(3) Enactment of other legislation by the State of Montana for the protection of environmental life support systems and prevention of waste are covered by the following citations: 
(a) State of Montana, Coal Conservation Act, 50-1601, RCM 1947.
(b) State of Montana, Strip Mine Siting Act; Title 50, Chapter 16, Section 1-17, RCM 1947.
(c) State of Montana, Open Cut Mining Act, 50-1018, RCM 1947.
(d) State of Montana, Montana Environmental Policy Act; Title 69, Chapter 65, Sections 1-18, RCM 1947.
The Montana Major Facility Siting Act would be of prime importance should any type of conversion facility be proposed near the leasehold.
